Three-time Juno Award-winning queer rock icon Carole Pope was singing openly about lesbian desire on daytime radio before the culture had any idea what to do with her. As frontwoman of Rough Trade, Pope tore through 1970s and ’80s Toronto with sexually charged lyrics, punk-glam swagger and a refusal to make herself more palatable. events.summary: In the 1960s, biologists introduced wolves to Coronation Island in Alaska after deer overran it and decimated the forest understory. The wolves ate all the deer and, with nothing left to eat, starved. About 50 years later, the wolves of Pleasant Island Alaska found themselves in a similar situation: living on an island in the Pacific with no deer left to eat. The wolves of Pleasant Island, however, have not died out. Instead, theyve broadened their palate to include sea otters. What scientists dont know is how widespread this surf-and-turf phenomenon is. events.summary: One of the most beloved operas ever written, La Traviata pairs soaring melodies with a deeply personal story of love and sacrifice. At its center is Violetta, an independent woman navigating desire, societal expectation, and the fragile possibility of happiness on her own terms. As romance and reality collide, Verdi’s luminous score reveals the emotional complexity of living authentically in a world determined to impose its rules. Tender, tragic, and timeless, the opera continues to resonate for its compassionate portrayal of Violetta’s vulnerability, resilience, courage as she chooses personal truth in the face of public judgment.

Then he met the unforgettable Negra Ester, beginning a passionate and turbulent romance that would inspire one of Chile’s most iconic theatrical works. Starring Daniel Muñoz and Carmen Gloria Bresky, YOU BROKE MY HEART unfolds to the irresistible rhythm of cueca chora. Earthy, romantic, and alive with music, the film celebrates Parra’s legacy and the artists who transformed everyday experience into an essential part of Chile’s cultural memory. Why We Chose This Film Because

Vittorio De Sica’s follow-up to his international triumph Bicycle Thieves is an enchanting neorealist fairy tale in which he combined his celebrated slice-of-life poetry with flights of graceful comedy and storybook fantasy. On the outskirts of Milan, a band of vagabonds work together to form a shantytown. When it is discovered that the land they occupy contains oil, however, it’s up to the cherubic orphan Totò (Francesco Golisano)—with some divine help—to save their community from greedy developers. Tipping their hats to the imaginative whimsy of Charles Chaplin and René Clair, De Sica and screenwriter Cesare Zavattini (adapting his own novel) craft a big-hearted ode to the nobility of everyday people

events.summary: SICK: A Year in Our Bodies Our bodies may be sick. Our lives are not over. Our stories deserve to be seen. SICK: A Year in Our Bodies is a fundraising showcase centering Portland-area sex workers living with chronic illness and disability—and the ways we have learned to survive in a world that wasn’t built in our favor. For many disabled and chronically ill people, traditional employment demands something our bodies cannot always promise: the same energy every day, rigid schedules, eight-hour shifts, limited rest, and the ability to simply push through. Sex work can offer something different—the ability to build work around our bodies instead of constantly punishing our bodies to fit the expectations of work. We are dancers. Performers.
events.title: Sick: a Year In Our Bodies - Fundraiser Showcase
